c.tagline: Loire-side city of mechanical elephants and Breton dukes.

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis are metered and marked by a lit roof sign; booking via app (Uber, Bolt, FreeNow) or the local Allô Taxi Nantes radio service is easy.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance.

hood_landmark.Île de Nantes: Machines of the Isle of Nantes

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets around Gare de Nantes and the Commerce tram hub, especially late at night.

hood_desc: The elegant 18th- and 19th-century core around the Graslin theatre, the ornate Passage Pommeraye arcade, and the Cours Cambronne; best for first-timers who want shops, cafes, and monuments all on foot.
Nantes' medieval quarter of half-timbered houses and cobbled lanes beside the Château des ducs de Bretagne, packed with bars, bistros, and the city's liveliest nightlife.

The reinvented river island where former shipyards have become galleries and creative studios, home to the Machines of the Isle mechanical elephant and the Carrousel des Mondes Marins; arty and family-friendly.
A leafy residential district north of the center along the Erdre, near the Jardin des Plantes, with calm streets and local markets; a quiet base close to the action.
A former working-class riverside village to the west, now a laid-back neighborhood known for its Sunday Marché de Chantenay and views over the Loire; a local, unhurried feel.
lodging: Auberge de Jeunesse HI Nantes La Manu

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout France.

transit.hours: Trams and the Busway run from around 4:30am to about 12:30am; the Luciole night-bus lines cover late nights on weekends.
transit.pay: The TAN network uses the reloadable LIBERTAN card or paper tickets bought at machines and tabacs; a single ticket costs €1.80 (about US$2) and is valid for one hour with transfers. A 24-hour pass is €5.90. Validate on board.

transit.m: Aéroport shuttle bus (Navette) to Nantes railway station & center, ~20 min
TAN bus line 98 + Tram line 3 to the center, ~40 min

tip.r: Service is included by law ('service compris'); rounding up or leaving ~5-10% for good service is appreciated but not expected.

landmarks: Les Machines de l'île (Grand Éléphant)
A twelve-meter mechanical elephant lumbers past steampunk workshops on a former shipyard island, the flagship of Nantes's gloriously eccentric machine menagerie.
Château des ducs de Bretagne
The moated castle of Brittany's dukes anchors the old town, its white-tufa courtyard hiding an excellent museum of Nantes history.
Cathédrale Saint-Pierre-et-Saint-Paul
A soaring Gothic cathedral in luminous white stone, sheltering the exquisite Renaissance tomb of François II, last Duke of Brittany.
Passage Pommeraye
A theatrical three-tiered shopping arcade from 1843, its grand staircase, statues and glass roof make it France's most beautiful covered passage.
Jardin des Plantes
A seven-hectare botanical wonderland facing the station, mixing century-old magnolias with playful Claude Ponti sculptures and immaculate Victorian greenhouses.
Mémorial de l'abolition de l'esclavage
A moving riverside memorial beneath the Loire quays, confronting Nantes's slave-trading past through two thousand engraved plaques and a contemplative underground walkway.
Place Royale
The elegant granite-and-tufa centerpiece of eighteenth-century Nantes, crowned by a fountain personifying the Loire and its tributaries.
Île de Versailles
A tranquil Japanese garden island on the Erdre river, all koi ponds, tea house and cherry blossoms minutes from downtown.
Musée d'arts de Nantes
A superbly renovated fine-arts palace whose collections sweep from Renaissance masters to Kandinsky beneath a striking marble-veiled contemporary extension.
Trentemoult
A former fishing village across the Loire, reached by river shuttle, whose narrow lanes of brightly painted cottages charm photographers at golden hour.

train.note: Gare de Nantes is on the eastern edge of the centre with exits on both the north and south sides, the south side now serving the rebuilt bus interchange. TGV inOui and Ouigo trains reach Paris Montparnasse in about 2 hours, with TER services along the Loire to Angers, Le Mans, Saint-Nazaire and the coast. One direct TGV a day runs through to Brussels-Midi via Lille without changing in Paris - it is the city's only cross-border train, so book early as it sells out. Everything else international means a change at Paris or Lille. Ouigo tickets are non-flexible and sold only through ouigo.com and SNCF Connect.

bus.note: Coaches use the new bus station on the south side of Nantes railway station at the Pole d'Echange Multimodal Gare Sud, 70 Boulevard de Berlin - note that FlixBus moved here in January 2026 and that departures between 23:30 and 04:30 leave from the kerb on Boulevard de Berlin instead. Barcelona is around 12 hours and Brussels about 8, so most of these are overnight runs. There is even a direct service to Manchester via the Channel, for which you need a passport and a UK visa or ETA. Regional Pays de la Loire coaches run under the Aleop brand and are paid for on board.

intl.to: Trentemoult & Roquettes (France) - Navibus Loire river shuttle from Gare Maritime, and the Erdre crossing

ferry.note: Nantes is 50 km up the Loire estuary and has no sea ferry terminal, but the city transport network runs Navibus river shuttles that count as ordinary tram-bus journeys on the same ticket. Lines N1 and N2 cross the Loire from the Gare Maritime quay to the village of Trentemoult in about 10 minutes, and N3 is a small passeur across the Erdre. Seasonal Loire estuary cruise boats also run down to Saint-Nazaire in summer. For crossings to the UK or Ireland the nearest ports are Saint-Malo and Roscoff, two to three hours away, served by Brittany Ferries (https://www.brittany-ferries.co.uk/).

half.name: Clisson
half.blurb: A town rebuilt in an Italianate style after the French Revolution, surrounded by Muscadet vineyards and a ruined medieval castle.

half.name: Guérande
half.blurb: A walled medieval town beside salt marshes where fleur de sel has been hand-harvested for centuries.

half.name: La Baule
half.blurb: A Belle Époque beach resort on a wide Atlantic bay, lined with a five-kilometer sand promenade.

half.name: Puy du Fou
half.blurb: A historical theme park with large-scale live shows recreating Viking raids, Roman gladiator fights, and medieval battles.
